ayahOccurrences.text: أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْكَهْفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا۟ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا عَجَبًا
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلْكَهْفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا۟ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا عَجَبًا

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: وَٱلرَّقِيمِ is in the derivative form: رَقِيمٌ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ر/ق/م   r–q–m speckles, speckled snake, markings, stripes, writings, dotting, to mark, to dot, to write; a great number; side of the valley, place where flood waters gather. الرَّقِيمُ ʾal‐raqım, classified under this root, is considered by some philologists to be a borrowing from Greek.

Of this root, 2 forms occur 3 times in the Qur’an:
رَقِيمٌ raqım 1 time and مَرْقُومٌ marqūm 2 times.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
رَقِيمٌ raqım [n.; quasi‐pass. part.] variously interpreted as the name of the town from which the Men of the Cave came; a plate of lead or stone upon which the name of those men were recorded, or the name of their dog

(18:9) أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْكَهْفِ وَالرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا مِنْ ءَايَاتِنَا عَجَبًا did you find the Companions in the Cave and ʾal‐Raqım, among all Our other signs, so wondrous?

entries.label: مَرْقُومٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مَرْقُومٌ marqūm [pass. part.] inscribed, written

(83:9) كِتَابٌ مَرْقُومٌ a clearly inscribed record.
